moments.text: Colour daylight camera looking down on bare, ridged mountain slopes: crosshair, corner brackets, a north marker, redaction boxes at the edges. The view drifts steadily.
The sensor slews fast across the slopes and settles on a new area.
A tiny bright white dot emerges just below the top redaction box, right of centre, and slides down and slightly right.
The view pans quickly right and the dot passes over the crosshair.
The sensor follows over ridged slopes; a small white dot shows near the crosshair at times but is hard to pick out on bright ground.
Clearest look: the white dot sits just below-right of the crosshair, then slips to its left as bright ridges sweep past.
The picture switches from colour to black-and-white: the sunlit slope pale, the shadowed gully dark. The dot can no longer be told apart.
The picture flashes white, then dark, then the black-and-white view returns. Use frame step.
Contrast jumps: the sunlit slope on the left turns almost solid white, then fades back toward grey over about ten seconds.

notes: Object is a few pixels wide; only distinguishable against shadowed ground. Colour FMV until 4:11.9, IR after.
